youtube.commentText:
Troy Jackson's review of JD Vance's Maine visit: "JD Vance is a dirtbag." The Vice President had flown in and told a community grieving a father ICE killed to "have a little bit of perspective."

The man Vance wants everyone to keep in perspective was Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, 25, from Bucaramanga, Colombia. He delivered food, cleaned buildings, adored his three-year-old daughter, and carried a work permit and a Social Security number.

On July 13, an ICE agent fired into his car in a Biddeford neighborhood, rammed it, and killed him.

Vance's response, on Maine soil, was to shrug and change the subject to drug overdoses. He promised the killing would be investigated. The family's lawyer says no federal agency has so much as called them.

Jackson did not shrug. The dead man "had a Social Security number, he had a job," he said. "He had a life. He had a family." It was Vance, he added, who ought to "have some damn perspective," because a rogue agency was dragging people out of their homes and the Vice President did not seem to know what was going on.

This is the fight Jackson has built his whole campaign on. He is a fifth-generation logger from Allagash who spent his career taking on corporations and billionaires, refuses corporate PAC and billionaire money, and tells voters flat out that working people keep getting screwed while the rich get richer.

He won a Trump district by twenty points saying it.

So he turned the question on Collins, who voted to hand ICE roughly $40 billion inside a $70 billion package with no strings attached, then refused to say she regrets it.

"What are you doing about it, Susan?" he asked. "I'm sick of your concerns."

In that same visit, Vance called Collins "the most independent member of the United States Senate." She votes with Donald Trump about 95% of the time.

That is the race in Maine. One of them signed the check that armed the agency. The other flew in to tell people to calm down. And the logger from Allagash is the only one of the three who said the dead man's name like it mattered.
